rationale.text: The test has one requirement with four routes, listed alike by the methodology and the glossary: caption, title, aria-label, or aria-labelledby pointing to a text passage. The entry is none. The test applies to data tables that have a title, and the glossary counts as one a table merely preceded or followed by a text passage that serves as its title. Whether a nearby heading or paragraph serves as a table's title is judgment, and so is whether a table element is a data table rather than a layout table (see 5.1.1). So a check could neither find every table the test applies to nor be sure that a table without any of the four means has a title at all. The glossary also accepts each means only in so far as assistive technologies correctly render it and associate it with the table, which no check on the page can establish. axe's table-fake-caption is tagged but not linked: it faults a table, chosen by axe's own data-table heuristic, whose first row is a single cell spanning every column, and it never looks at caption, title, aria-label or aria-labelledby, so it examines none of the routes. axe also marks it experimental. Applicability is judgment. Needs holds assistive_tech, because of the glossary's condition on rendering by assistive technologies.
